title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
statement:
Suppose an array of length `n` sorted in ascending order is rotated between `1` and `n` times. Given the rotated sorted array `nums` of unique elements, return the minimum element of the array.

You must write an algorithm that runs in `O(log n)` time.

Compare `nums[mid]` with `nums[right]`: if `nums[mid] > nums[right]`, the minimum lies strictly to the right of `mid`; otherwise the minimum is at `mid` or to its left.
constraints: All the integers of nums are unique
nums is sorted and rotated between 1 and n times

editorial.approach: Binary search with `left = 0` and `right = nums.length - 1`. At each step compute `mid`. If `nums[mid] > nums[right]`, the array's minimum must be to the right of `mid` (since a rotation boundary exists between them), so set `left = mid + 1`. Otherwise the minimum is at `mid` or somewhere to its left, so set `right = mid` (not `mid - 1`, since `mid` itself could be the answer). The loop ends when `left === right`, which points to the minimum.
